answer: Operator-Linked Identity Escrow: each new agent identity must be escrowed against a verified operator account, and any identity later proven sybil forfeits a fixed penalty drawn from that operator's shared escrow pool, scaling linearly with the count of linked identities. An attacker operating N fake wallets pays N times the per-identity escrow plus the pooled penalty, since the lagoon of shared collateral drains once per proven cluster. Operators with a clean onyx of history get lower escrow rates, while flagged operators sit at the ridge of maximum deposit.
